bug_description.original: The function KAr::openArchive in the relevant file is vulnerable to invalid memory access when handling broken files.
bug_description.normalized: The staged witness is parsed as an ar archive by `KAr::openArchive()`. Its first relevant member header is the special `//` longfilename-table entry, but the header's blank size field parses as `size = 0`, so the parser allocates `ar_longnames` as a 1-byte NUL-only buffer. The next header is treated as a longfilename reference; its `name` field starts with `/` and its numeric suffix is converted to offset 8. The vulnerable code checks only that `ar_longnames` is non-null, then executes `name = &ar_longnames[name.mid(1, 15).toInt()]` without checking that the parsed offset fits within the longfilename table. `QByteArray::operator=(char const*)` immediately reads from the resulting out-of-bounds pointer, producing the observed AddressSanitizer heap-buffer-overflow read.

source.description: First project-code statement on the vulnerable path that reads a full ar member header from the attacker-controlled buffer into parser state.
source.value_from: After the witness passes the `!<arch>` main-magic check, this read materializes the first 60-byte member header. In the staged `poc`, that header is the `//` special entry whose blank size field later parses as `size = 0` and seeds the undersized longfilename-table allocation.

relation.description: Source identity relation for the vulnerability-relevant value.

tainted_value_origin.description: The attacker controls the bytes loaded into `ar_header` on each relevant loop iteration. Those bytes produce both critical values in the witness: the first header's parsed longfilename-table size `0`, and the second header's longfilename-reference string whose numeric suffix is later converted to offset `8`.

root_cause.description: The parser converts the attacker-controlled longfilename reference to an integer and uses it as an `ar_longnames` index without checking that the offset is within the allocated longfilename-table extent.
root_cause.note: The only preceding guard is `if (! ar_longnames)`, which proves only that a table pointer exists. The relevant fix hoists the parsed suffix into `ar_longnamesIndex` and, on this witness where the current header's blank size field also parses to `0`, rejects `8 >= size` before this assignment; the same patch hunk also adds a separate negative-size check, but the witnessed crash is the unchecked longfilename offset dereference.

sink.description: ASan crash site. Assigning from the out-of-bounds `char *` invokes `QByteArray::operator=(char const*)`, which reads from the invalid longfilename-table pointer until NUL.
sink.note: The saved sanitizer trace reports `READ of size 1` in `QByteArray::operator=(char const*)` at this line and places the faulting address `0x602000000078` 7 bytes to the right of the 1-byte allocation made at `kar.cpp:146`.

parser_admitted.description: The staged witness begins with the 7-byte magic `!<arch>`, so `KAr::openArchive()` does not return `Invalid main magic` and proceeds into the member-header loop.

fine_trace.note: On the first relevant loop iteration after the `!<arch>` check and alignment seek, `KAr::openArchive()` reads the first 60-byte attacker-controlled member header into `ar_header`. This header seeds the longfilename-table state used later in the crash.
Parsing that first header yields `name` beginning with `//`, so the entry is treated as the longfilename table, and the blank size field parses to `size = 0`.

Because `size` is `0`, the longfilename-table branch allocates `ar_longnames` with `size + 1 == 1` byte, writes `ar_longnames[0] = '\0'`, and reads zero table payload bytes. ASan later identifies this exact 1-byte heap allocation as the overflowed region.

Because the longfilename table consumed zero bytes, the next 60 input bytes are immediately read as the following member header. This second header is the longfilename-reference entry that drives the out-of-bounds access.

Parsing the second header yields a `name` field that begins with `/`, selecting the longfilename-reference case. For the staged witness, the numeric suffix in that field is the attacker-controlled reference string that `name.mid(1, 15).toInt()` later resolves to offset `8`.

The only guard before dereferencing a longfilename reference checks that a table pointer exists. Step 3 made `ar_longnames` non-null, so control falls through; there is still no check that the parsed reference fits within the 0-byte longfilename table.

The second header's reference suffix is converted to integer `8` and used as an `ar_longnames` index without any bounds check. With only the 1-byte allocation from step 3 available, this computes the out-of-bounds pointer `&ar_longnames[8]`.

Assigning that invalid `char *` to `QByteArray name` invokes `QByteArray::operator=(char const*)`, which reads from the out-of-bounds address until it finds a NUL byte. ASan reports the resulting `READ of size 1` 7 bytes past the 1-byte allocation from step 3.

allocation_context.note: ASan reports the faulting address relative to the allocation made by `new char[size + 1]`; for the staged witness, `size` parsed as `0`, so the live heap region is only 1 byte long.

sanitizer_ground_truth.source: parsed from staged sanitizer_trace.txt, default_crash_trace.txt, and reproduction_report.json

cross_validation.patch_resolves_note: The staged patch hoists the parsed suffix into `ar_longnamesIndex` and rejects when `ar_longnamesIndex >= size` immediately before the crashing assignment. On this witness, the second header's size field is also blank, so that current-entry `size` parses to `0`; with parsed offset `8`, the new `8 >= size` check fails and returns before `QByteArray::operator=(char const*)` can read from `&ar_longnames[8]`.

poc.trigger: The staged `poc` is the exact 128-byte witness saved by Stage 01. It begins with `!<arch>`, then presents a `//` longfilename-table header whose blank size field parses as `0`, followed immediately by a second header whose `/...` name field becomes longfilename offset `8`. When `karchive_fuzzer` opens that buffer in read-only mode, `KAr::openArchive()` allocates a 1-byte `ar_longnames` buffer and then crashes at `src/kar.cpp:162` while assigning `name = &ar_longnames[8]`.

format.name: malformed ar archive with zero-length longfilename table
format.contract: A buffer that `KAr::openArchive()` accepts as an ar archive, whose first relevant member is the special `//` longfilename-table entry with a blank size field so `size == 0`, and whose next relevant member is a longfilename reference whose numeric suffix is parsed as `8`. This witness-specific combination produces `&ar_longnames[8]` from a 1-byte allocation and triggers the observed ASan heap-buffer-overflow read.
